basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 3:12 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 74. Cur Adam peccatum in mulierem detorsit (Gen. III, 12) ?-- Resp. Ad cumulum'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 74. Cur Adam peccatum in mulierem detorsit (Gen. III, 12) ?-- Resp. Ad cumulum peccati sui superbe respondit, [et] non humiliter; quasi querimoniam in Deum dirigeret cur ei talem dedisset sociam, unde ei peccati occasio esset. Similiter et mulier suae culpae causam in creatorem refert, quare [ Al., quia] serpentem, per quem deciperetur [in paradiso] creaverit.
